newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare gains in pale Wall St. echo.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare gains in pale Wall St. echo.

text.p: Mexican stocks trimmed earlier moderate gains at slow midday dealing on what dealers said was a scaled-down reflection of trends on Wall Street in an uncertain market.
"Trading is dull. Prices are at a level which are expensive for buyers, but not high enough for sellers," a floor trader said. "The Dow is still high, but not nearly as much as before."
The leading IPC share index was up 2.02 points, or 0.05 percent, at 4,128.32. Trading volume was unremarkable at 42.3 million shares.
The IPC had reached as high as 4,140.71 points in early trade.
The Dow Jones was meanwhile up 45.36 points to 7523.86, albeit off a trading record set earlier at 7,572.30.
Dealers said an unexpected recovery by the peso from last week's slide had kept foreign investors away.
"Several foreign brokers are selling. A firmer peso means it's a good time for them to sell, rather than to buy," the floor trader added.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 0.65 of a centavo firmer on the day at 7.9730/7.9760.
Dealers added that most of the few buyers in the market were local brokers, with demand concentrated on financial stocks and those benefitting from recent corporate news.
Some dealers financial stocks were in demand on speculation over a possible forthcoming government plan to restructure mortgage debts.
Shares listed by Mexico's two largest financial groups, Bancomer and Banacci accounted for 29 percent of all shares traded at mid-session.
Bancomer B shares were up one centavo to 3.38 pesos, while its A shares were unchanged at 1.86 pesos.
Banacci B shares had meanwhile shed 12 centavos to 18.68 pesos on what dealers said was profit-taking from recent gains.
Dealers noted primary interest rates were expected to increase at Tuesday evening's central bank auction, but said the market had already discounted this move.
Corn flour and tortilla maker Maseca was up 26 centavos to 7.86 pesos following Monday's announcement of a change in a government scheme to subsidize what in Mexico is a basic staple.
On the broad market, 98 stocks had changed hands, of which sliders outnumbered gainers by 43 to 33.
